summary: The sample implements the core requested behavior: a Python LangChain-based ingestion pipeline that extracts sentiment/topics/quote, computes and stores embeddings, and runs aggregation pipelines to surface net sentiment by channel, topic and time. The repository contains both the Beanie/Motor async code paths and a synchronous pymongo fallback; the run artifacts and README reflect the choices the builder recorded in decisions.jsonl. Major functional items from the starter prompt are met. Several gallery-quality items are missing or only partially implemented (index-parameter guidance, a /search API and similarity-score return, test infra without a live cluster, full dependency pinning for all code paths, and IaC for provisioning). The most important operational gap observed at build time (and recorded by the builder) is that some Python dependency builds (pydantic-core) can fail on modern Pythons; the builder included a runnable pymongo fallback but also left the Beanie code in the tree. See requirement_results, practice checks and doc_gaps for details and the smallest fixes to reach gallery quality.

requirement_results.requirement: Use Python with LangChain to build a single agent that takes each incoming feedback item through the whole flow: ingest, extract, embed and store.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:20-58 shows enrich_and_store using ChatOpenAI and OpenAIEmbeddings (LangChain) and inserting a Feedback document; app/src/scripts/seed.py and app/scripts/seed.py call the enrichment flow.

requirement_results.requirement: Accept customer feedback from more than one channel and carry each item's source channel through to the stored document.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/scripts/seed.py:10-16 contains sample items with channels (email, chat, survey); app/src/ingest.py:49-56 sets channel and source_id on the Feedback document.

requirement_results.requirement: Use prompt engineering (LangChain prompts sent to an LLM) to extract from each feedback text its sentiment, its key topics and a verbatim quote taken from the original text.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:15-18 defines EXTRACTION_PROMPT; app/src/ingest.py:29-39 calls the ChatOpenAI LLM and parses JSON.

requirement_results.requirement: Compute an embedding of the feedback text and store the resulting vector on the document.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:43-56 uses OpenAIEmbeddings.embed_documents and stores embedding on Feedback; app/src/app/processor.py provides a deterministic_embedding fallback used when embeddings fail.

requirement_results.requirement: Define the enriched feedback document as a Beanie ODM model and persist it to Azure DocumentDB through Beanie, holding the original text, the source channel, when the feedback was received, the extracted sentiment, key topics and verbatim quote, and the embedding.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/models.py:6-15 defines class Feedback(Document) with channel, source_id, text, sentiment, topics, quote, embedding, created_at; app/src/ingest.py:49-58 constructs Feedback and await doc.insert().

requirement_results.requirement: Build an aggregation pipeline, run in Azure DocumentDB through Beanie's aggregation API, that surfaces a net sentiment measure per channel.
requirement_results.evidence: app/scripts/run_aggregations.py:8-16 uses Feedback.get_motor_collection().aggregate with $group by $channel computing avgSentiment.

requirement_results.requirement: Build an aggregation pipeline, run in Azure DocumentDB, that surfaces net sentiment per key topic.
requirement_results.evidence: app/scripts/run_aggregations.py:18-24 unwinds $topics and groups by topic, computing avgSentiment.

requirement_results.requirement: Build an aggregation pipeline, run in Azure DocumentDB, that surfaces net sentiment over time by bucketing feedback into time periods.
requirement_results.evidence: app/scripts/run_aggregations.py:29-36 groups by formatted date ($dateToString on created_at) to compute avg sentiment per day.

requirement_results.requirement: The connection string and model credentials come from environment variables; none appear in the repository.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py:9 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI from env; app/src/ingest.py:11-13 reads OPENAI_API_KEY/EMBEDDING_MODEL/LLM_MODEL from env; app/.env.example contains placeholders rather than real secrets.

requirement_results.requirement: A .env.example lists every setting with placeholder values.
requirement_results.evidence: app/.env.example:2-9 lists DOCUMENTDB_URI, OPENAI_API_KEY, EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIM, LLM_MODEL and DATABASE_NAME placeholders.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index dimensions match the embedding model's output.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:75 uses int(os.getenv('EMBEDDING_DIM','1536')) when creating the search index; app/src/ingest.py:12-13 sets default EMBEDDING_MODEL='text-embedding-3-small' and app/.env.example sets EMBEDDING_DIM=1536. The code lets the user override EMBEDDING_DIM to match their chosen model.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Document in README a specific, paired default mapping (EMBEDDING_MODEL -> EMBEDDING_DIM) and add a runtime check that validates the embedding length returned by the embedder against EMBEDDING_DIM before index creation.

requirement_results.requirement: The vector index parameters are chosen for the sample's data size, and the README says how to change them for a larger one.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:66-88 creates an embedding index with default type 'vector-hnsw' but does not set HNSW tuning parameters (M, efConstruction) nor does README.md provide guidance for tuning these for larger datasets (app/README.md lines 27-28 mention index creation but give no parameter guidance).
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add default index-parameter values for small seed datasets to create_search_indexes (e.g., M=16, efConstruction=100) and a short paragraph in README explaining how to increase them for larger data and the tradeoffs.

requirement_results.requirement: One database client is created and reused across requests.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/db.py:14-19 implements an AsyncIOMotorClient singleton _client; app/src/app/db.py:8-15 implements a synchronous MongoClient singleton for the fallback path.

requirement_results.requirement: A seed script loads sample data and creates the index, and can be run twice without duplicating data.
requirement_results.evidence: app/src/scripts/seed.py:26-35 checks Feedback.find_one(Feedback.source_id == item['source_id']) and only calls enrich_and_store if the source_id is absent; create_search_indexes is called once before inserts.

requirement_results.requirement: /search returns a clear error for an empty query and when the embedding call fails.
requirement_results.evidence: No /search HTTP endpoint or CLI search wrapper is present in the repository; create_search_indexes and aggregation scripts exist but there is no search API implementation to validate error behavior.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a simple search wrapper (e.g., FastAPI route /search) that validates input (non-empty query), calls the embedder, catches embedding failures, and returns clear 4xx/5xx responses with error messages and logging.

requirement_results.requirement: Search results include the similarity score.
requirement_results.evidence: No search query code that performs vector similarity queries is present; app/scripts/run_aggregations.py prints aggregation results but there is no nearest-neighbour search implementation returning scores.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Implement a search function that queries $search / cosmosSearch and returns the score alongside documents; document the field name used for the score.

requirement_results.requirement: Dependencies are pinned in requirements.txt.
requirement_results.evidence: app/requirements.txt pins pymongo, python-dotenv and pytest (app/requirements.txt:1-3). The repository contains Beanie/Motor/LangChain/OpenAI imports in app/src/* but these are not pinned in app/requirements.txt.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a requirements-beanie.txt and requirements-run.txt (or a single consolidated requirements.txt) that pins the versions used by the primary code paths (beanie, motor, pydantic-core, langchain, openai) and list an alternative lightweight pinned set for the minimal/pymongo fallback.

requirement_results.requirement: Unit tests run without a live cluster.
requirement_results.evidence: There are no unit tests in the repository and pytest.ini exists (app/pytest.ini) but no tests are present to assert offline behavior or use mocks for the DB/embedding/LLM calls.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add unit tests that mock the Motor/Mongo client and LangChain embedder/LLM (pytest + pytest-mock) so tests run without a live cluster; include these in CI instructions.

requirement_results.requirement: Infrastructure for the cluster is provided as code, using the Azure DocumentDB resource type.
requirement_results.evidence: No IaC (Bicep/Terraform/az CLI templates) exists in the repository; the sample README and code assume an existing cluster provided via DOCUMENTDB_URI.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a small 'iac' folder containing a Bicep or Terraform snippet showing Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters with low-cost defaults and a README note explaining that it is optional and must be run by an operator with appropriate permissions.

requirement_results.requirement: The README covers what the sample shows, prerequisites, setup, run, and clean-up.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md lines 1-22 cover what the sample shows, prerequisites and quickstart; it does not include explicit clean-up steps to remove sample data or cluster resources.
requirement_results.smallest_fix: Add a 'clean-up' section that shows how to delete the sample documents or drop the 'feedback' collection and how to tear down any IaC-provisioned resources if included.

requirement_results.requirement: The sample uses the name "Azure DocumentDB" throughout, and no former or neighbouring product name.
requirement_results.evidence: app/README.md and code refer to 'Azure DocumentDB' and environment var DOCUMENTDB_URI; no evidence of Cosmos DB or Amazon DocumentDB naming in the sample files.

checks.practice: Keep the cluster connection string out of source control and read it from environment variables; use a secret store for production.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:9-15 reads DOCUMENTDB_URI via os.getenv and raises if missing; app/.env.example provides a placeholder.

sources.title: Migrate from Amazon DocumentDB to Azure DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)

checks.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient/driver client per process.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:12-19 implements an AsyncIOMotorClient singleton; app/src/app/db.py:6-15 implements a sync MongoClient singleton for the fallback.

checks.practice: Always connect with TLS and do not disable certificate validation in production.
checks.evidence: app/src/db.py:18 constructs AsyncIOMotorClient(..., tls=True, retryWrites=False).

checks.practice: Implement retries for transient faults with exponential backoff and respect Retry-After.
checks.evidence: No general retry middleware is present in the sample code for DB operations or embedding/LLM calls; specific calls wrap exceptions but do not implement exponential backoff (app/src/ingest.py:29-47 and app/src/ingest.py:43-47 catch exceptions and fall back).
checks.what_would_help: A short example in the driver skill showing how to wrap LangChain/embedder and Motor operations in a retry decorator (with exponential backoff and honoring Retry-After) would let an agent add this automatically.

checks.practice: Use cluster tier / vCore and storage sizing (M-tiers) for indexing/vector workloads (not RU/s).
checks.evidence: Sample does not provision or manage cloud resources in code and reads DOCUMENTDB_URI pointing to an existing cluster; provisioning guidance is outside this sample's scope.
checks.source: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Create single-field and compound indexes for fields used in filters and grouping (channel, created_at).
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:92-96 (fallback) creates a text index on 'text'; aggregation scripts assume indexes on created_at and channel for performance but sample does not explicitly create those single-field indexes—the create_search_indexes function creates search indexes and the fallback only creates a text index.
checks.fix: Add explicit single-field indexes for channel and created_at if the sample expects them: e.g., ensure db.feedback.create_index([('channel',1)]), db.feedback.create_index([('created_at',1)]).

checks.practice: Use TTL indexes to implement time-based retention.
checks.evidence: The sample does not include a retention policy or TTL index; it targets small sample data and demonstrates aggregation not retention.

checks.practice: Store embeddings as number[] with fixed dimensionality and embedder metadata; normalize if using cosine.
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:55-56 stores embedding on Feedback; app/.env.example defines EMBEDDING_DIM and app/src/app/processor.py enforces EMBEDDING_DIM during deterministic embedding; no explicit per-document embedder metadata field was found.
checks.fix: Add embedder metadata fields (e.g., embedding_model, embedding_dim) to the Feedback model and write them at insert time so index and queries can validate dimensions.

checks.practice: Pick index type to match scale and tune HNSW/IVF/DiskANN parameters.
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:66-88 chooses 'vector-hnsw' with only dimensions and similarity; it does not set HNSW tuning params (M, efConstruction) or document tradeoffs in README.
checks.fix: Set explicit HNSW parameters suitable for the sample (e.g., M=16, efConstruction=100) and add README guidance on how to change them for larger datasets.

checks.practice: If createSearchIndexes isn't available, implement a graceful fallback (store embeddings and client-side NN).
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:61-96 wraps db.command(idx_body) in try/except and falls back to coll.create_index([('text','text')]) and the builder recorded that the live cluster returned CommandNotSupported (builder_report / decisions). app/src/app/processor.py provides deterministic_embedding for offline local runs.
checks.searched: Search for createSearchIndexes CommandNotSupported fallback in Microsoft docs returned no clear authoritative guidance; discovery recorded 'prior_knowledge_only'.
checks.what_would_help: A public Microsoft Learn note describing the createSearchIndexes availability and a recommended fallback recipe would help agents pick a robust fallback automatically.

checks.practice: Prefer atomic update/patch operations ($set) rather than full document replaces when enriching records.
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:49-58 constructs a full Feedback model and calls await doc.insert() rather than update/patch on an existing raw document; the seed script uses upsert-like logic by checking existence, but there is no explicit $set-based enrichment path for an existing raw record.
checks.source: Understand request units consumption in Azure Cosmos DB
checks.fix: When enriching an existing raw record, use an update with $set for sentiment/topics/embedding fields (e.g., collection.update_one({'_id': id}, {'$set': {...}})) so large rewrites are avoided.

sources.title: Understand request units consumption in Azure Cosmos DB

checks.practice: Use bulk operations (insertMany / bulkWrite) for batch ingestion.
checks.evidence: Sample uses per-item enrich_and_store for the small seed set and does not implement batch bulk ingestion; the seed path inserts only five items incrementally.
checks.source: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Enforce lightweight JSON Schema validation at the collection level ($jsonSchema).
checks.evidence: No collection-level JSON Schema validation or $jsonSchema validator is created in create_search_indexes or seed scripts; the sample assumes feedback shape but does not set server-side validation.
checks.fix: Add a collection create/modify step that sets a $jsonSchema validator requiring text, channel, created_at and embedding length (or validate in application before insert).

checks.practice: Store embedding metadata (model name and dimension) with each vector and rebuild indexes on model change.
checks.evidence: Feedback model (app/src/models.py:6-15) includes embedding: Optional[List[float]] but does not include embedding_model or embedding_dim metadata fields; .env.example and code mention EMBEDDING_MODEL/EMBEDDING_DIM but per-document metadata is not written.
checks.fix: Add embedding_model and embedding_dim fields to the Feedback document and populate them at write time so downstream searches can detect mismatches.

checks.practice: Enable diagnostic settings, slow-query logs and use explain() for pipelines.
checks.evidence: The sample is a small demo and does not configure cluster-level diagnostic settings or run explain() on queries; these are operator / cluster concerns rather than sample code.

checks.practice: Use Private Endpoint / firewall rules to restrict access to your cluster.
checks.evidence: Sample runs against an externally reachable cluster; network controls are an operational configuration outside the sample code.
checks.source: Enable private access in Azure DocumentDB

sources.title: Enable private access in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: Prefer createSearchIndexes + $search over community $text.
checks.evidence: app/src/ingest.py:61-96 attempts db.command(createSearchIndexes) and falls back to a text index only if the command is rejected; README documents the intention (app/README.md:27-28).

checks.practice: Use deterministic document IDs or composite keys and upsert semantics to make ingestion idempotent.
checks.evidence: app/src/scripts/seed.py:26-34 checks for existing Feedback by source_id and does not duplicate; Feedback model includes source_id. The seed path uses existence check rather than atomic upsert but achieves idempotence for the provided sample.
checks.source: Insert data into Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB
checks.fix: Consider switching the seed insertion to an upsert (replace_one(filter, update, upsert=True)) keyed on source_id/_id for stronger idempotence.

sources.title: Insert data into Azure Cosmos DB for MongoDB

checks.practice: Store timestamps in UTC as Date/ISODate and index the timestamp field for time-window aggregations.
checks.evidence: app/src/models.py:14 defines created_at: datetime defaulting to datetime.utcnow(); aggregation pipelines in app/scripts/run_aggregations.py use created_at in grouping (app/scripts/run_aggregations.py:32).
checks.source: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB (indexing guidance) / Indexing Strategies

sources.title: Document size and batch write limits in Azure DocumentDB (indexing guidance) / Indexing Strategies

checks.practice: Avoid storing raw PII in cleartext; use pseudonymization/encryption/masking.
checks.evidence: Sample data contains only generic sample text and no explicit PII handling code; the code does not attempt PII detection/redaction before indexing. Whether PII appears depends on real user data and deployment policies.
checks.source: Security Frame: Sensitive Data | Mitigations / Data encryption in Azure DocumentDB
checks.fix: If real production data will be ingested, add a PII-detection step and either mask or encrypt sensitive fields before storing or document that the sample is intended for non-PII data only.

sources.title: Security Frame: Sensitive Data | Mitigations / Data encryption in Azure DocumentDB

checks.practice: When enriching with LLMs store source_text, extracted fields, and model metadata so reprocessing is possible.
checks.evidence: Feedback model (app/src/models.py) stores text, topics, quote and embedding but does not include model metadata (LLM_MODEL, EMBEDDING_MODEL, or version) per-document; app/src/ingest.py uses process-time LLM/embedding env vars but does not persist them alongside the stored document.
checks.searched: Searches for authoritative public guidance about storing per-document LLM model metadata returned no clear Microsoft Learn page; discovery flagged this as prior_knowledge_only.
checks.fix: Add fields to Feedback for llm_model, embedding_model and embedding_dim and write them when storing the document so future reprocessing can detect model changes.
checks.what_would_help: A short Microsoft Learn page recommending per-document embedder/LLM metadata would let agents add this by default.

decision_reviews.comment: A readiness approval; nothing to verify in code. Decision matches the run artifacts (the build proceeded).
Choosing Python is consistent with the repository and the prompt. Code is Python-based and uses LangChain/Beanie imports.
The builder recorded the Beanie+Motor choice in app/src/models.py and app/src/db.py. The code contains those files and initializers.

Choosing 'text-embedding-3-small' and EMBEDDING_DIM=1536 is a model-default choice (reason_source=model_default). It is a reasonable default but not mandated by any Microsoft docs; the decision is a builder preference and cannot be judged "correct" against a public standard.
Choosing gpt-3.5-turbo as default LLM is a model_default decision and is acceptable as a sample choice; it is not verifiable against a product doc.
The code reads secrets from environment variables (app/.env.example, app/src/db.py, app/src/ingest.py). The .env.example was created.
The repository assumes an existing cluster via DOCUMENTDB_URI and does not contain IaC; this matches the decision not to provision resources.
The code attempts createSearchIndexes (app/src/ingest.py:66-89) and includes a fallback; this matches the documented choice.
Duplicate readiness approval; consistent with D001.
Selecting Python 3.11 is consistent with README and code comments; acceptable as a builder choice.

The decision to use Beanie+Motor is present in code, but events/decisions show the builder later recorded problems building pydantic-core and ultimately added a synchronous pymongo fallback. The repository therefore contains both the Beanie code and fallback code (app/src and app/src/app). The decision is defensible but the environment forced a change the builder recorded.
Model_default decision to prefer OpenAI embeddings with deterministic fallback; a valid sample choice but not verifiable against product documentation.
Model_default decision for LLM with a deterministic fallback; acceptable but not grounded in product docs.

Decision to attempt createSearchIndexes and to fall back on failure is implemented in app/src/ingest.py:61-96 and matches the builder report that the live cluster returned CommandNotSupported and the code handled it.
Secrets read from env vars and .env.example exists (app/.env.example).

The builder recorded swapping Beanie versions during pip attempts; pip output is recorded as reason_source 'tool_result' in decisions.jsonl and the repository shows Beanie-based code still present. The decision itself (selecting an available beanie version) is a tool-driven choice.

The builder recorded switching to Motor+pymongo-only due to pydantic-core build failures; the repository contains a synchronous pymongo fallback (app/src/app/db.py, app/src/app/models.py, app/src/app/processor.py) consistent with that. The events/03-build notes and build report also document pip failures.

The repository contains synchronous pymongo-based singleton (app/src/app/db.py) and synchronous processing helpers (app/src/app/processor.py) consistent with the recorded decision to switch to pymongo for runnable verification in this environment.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Authoritative guidance pairing common embedding models (OpenAI/Azure/other) with their output dimensions and recommended ENV names (EMBEDDING_MODEL -> EMBEDDING_DIM) so samples can set correct defaults.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Skills and Microsoft Learn; readiness findings recorded this gap (no single authoritative mapping page found).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder picked a reasonable default (text-embedding-3-small / 1536) but the choice is a model_default and must be documented for users to avoid silent dimension mismatches when they change providers.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short Microsoft Learn page or sample README section titled 'Embedding model names and dimensions' listing common models (text-embedding-3-small:1536, text-embedding-3-large:1536, all-MiniLM-L6-v2:384, etc.), the env var names (EMBEDDING_MODEL, EMBEDDING_DIM), and a runtime validation snippet to assert the embedder returns the expected length.

doc_gaps.topic: Index parameter defaults for small samples
doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Concrete default ANN tuning parameters (HNSW M / efConstruction, DiskANN lBuild / lSearch) for small sample datasets and instructions on when/how to increase them for production.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-vector-search skill and Microsoft Learn vector-search docs; the skill gives theory but no sample-size defaults.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: create_search_indexes in the sample used vector-hnsw but omitted explicit tuning; users won't know safe default values to start with and may misconfigure for larger scales.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'Vector index tuning for sample vs production' guide: recommended values for <10k docs (HNSW M=8-16, efConstruction=100), for 10k-100k (M=16-32, efConstruction=200), and for production (DiskANN) with examples of how to change createSearchIndexes payload and the tradeoffs.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Clear guidance on driver/ODM compatibility: whether Beanie remains the recommended ODM and whether Motor vs AsyncPyMongo is preferred for DocumentDB, and examples for both stacks.
doc_gaps.where_searched: documentdb-driver skill and Beanie docs; no authoritative statement reconciles the two.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builder attempted Beanie+Motor, encountered pydantic-core build issues and introduced a pymongo fallback; a clearer note would let agents choose a path that is broadly reproducible in typical developer runtimes.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: A short page 'Python ODM recommendations for Azure DocumentDB' showing 1) Beanie+Motor example and its pinned versions, 2) AsyncPyMongo+ODM alternative, and 3) a note on pydantic-core build constraints with recommended Python versions.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A dedicated Microsoft Learn note that states which cluster types/tiers support createSearchIndexes and a canonical fallback recipe when the command returns CommandNotSupported (store embeddings + client-side NN or fallback text index).
doc_gaps.where_searched: Search queries for createSearchIndexes availability returned no single authoritative page documenting all scenarios; discovery returned prior_knowledge_only for fallback guidance.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The builder handled the cluster returning CommandNotSupported, but an agent without this workaround would have failed to produce the demo outputs or would have stopped the build.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Page titled 'Search index availability and fallbacks' that: (a) lists createSearchIndexes supported SKUs/tiers, (b) gives copy-paste index-creation JSON and expected errors when unsupported, and (c) prescribes a fallback implementation (store embeddings + example client-side approximate-NN snippet) and sample code.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A clear, prominent statement on the overview / quickstart pages explaining that Azure DocumentDB (vCore) uses M-tier (vCore) compute + storage billing and not Cosmos DB RU/s.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Readiness findings and skills; this confusion surfaced repeatedly in the readiness report where cold answers used RU/s.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: Builders might use the wrong provisioning model or IaC resource type leading to wrong CLI/Bicep usage and failed deployments.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Add a 'How this product is billed' section to the Azure DocumentDB overview with a one-line comparison to Cosmos RU billing and explicit examples of the correct resource type (Microsoft.DocumentDB/mongoClusters) and CLI commands (az documentdb mongocluster).

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: Guidance recommending adding llm_model, embedding_model and embedding_dim metadata to documents when storing LLM/extraction results, and instructions to re-index when models change.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Skills and Microsoft Learn returned no dedicated page for this LLM-integrated sample pattern (searches listed in discovered_practices).
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: The sample stores embeddings and extracted fields but does not persist model metadata per document; this makes safe reprocessing or detecting model/embedding-dimension drift harder.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Short 'LLM + embedder metadata' guidance with example Beanie/Mongo fields, code to write metadata at enrichment time, and a re-index checklist for when you change embedding dimensions or model.

doc_gaps.what_was_missing: A small test scaffold and examples demonstrating how to run unit tests without a live cluster using mocking/stubs for Motor/pymongo and LangChain.
doc_gaps.where_searched: Repo and skills; the sample lacks offline tests and the skill docs don't include a test scaffold snippet for this exact scenario.
doc_gaps.effect_on_this_build: No unit tests were added; maintainers and reviewers cannot run automated checks locally without setting up a cluster or mocking strategy.
doc_gaps.proposed_content: Agent-kit rule and sample test code: provide pytest fixtures that monkeypatch the DB client and the langchain embedder/LLM; example tests for analyze_and_prepare, deterministic_embedding and enrich_and_store (mocked).
